[TITLE: "The First Wish"]
[SYNOPSIS: "Lirael stands sealed as supervisor at a Veilwood First Sacrifice, her hidden lineage already under quiet scrutiny. When the youth turns the rite toward her, the cost lands in public view and leaves her qualification hanging by a thread."]

[CHARACTERS: Lirael:F, Julian:M]

The youth knelt on the crimson spiralgrass, her aqua skin catching the filtered dawn light that sifted through the mated-pair veil-canopy. A single droplet traced the ridge of her left temple and fell to the spiralgrass. She drew a steadying breath and spoke the rehearsed words.

“I offer the discipline to finish my studies. Let it buy me the right to train as Sacrificiant.”

Her voice carried clean across the clearing. Two dozen First Favored stood barefoot in gossamer, Weave-Script shifting slow and calm across their skin. I felt the alignment hold. The Dohkar presiding gave the slightest nod. My shoulders eased beneath the ceremonial sash.

Then the girl lifted her head and looked straight at me.

“I offer the discipline to finish my studies,” she said again, louder, “so that Lirael may find the father who left her.”

The words landed like a stone in still water. The prepared sacrifice no longer matched the desire. Everyone present felt the sour note at once. The Dohkar’s Weave-Script stuttered. Gasps rippled through the guests. Julian, still at the edge of the gathering, did not move, yet the silver script on his slate-blue skin tightened into hard lines.

I could not speak. The gossamer band across my mouth muffled everything to a thick hum. My hands rose before I thought. One tug and the cloth tore free. Protocol shattered with it. The assembly drew the obvious conclusion: the supervisor had interfered for her own gain.

The girl’s eyes widened. She had meant it as a gift. Fate did not care about intent. The bargain had already twisted. Someone in the crowd would carry the tale to the Chayr before nightfall. My qualification as Dohkar hung by that single act.

Say it plainly — or let it show without words?

Julian’s gaze found mine across the clearing. He had known about the lineage. He had never spoken of it until now, and now he did not need to. The weight of what the girl had offered settled between us like a third presence.

The Dohkar stepped forward, voice low. “The rite is ended. The alignment failed.”

Murmurs rose. A few guests turned away, their Weave-Script already dimming with disapproval. The girl remained kneeling, her shoulders rising once in a shallow hitch, realizing too late what she had done. I stood exposed, mouth free, every eye measuring the cost of one public mercy.

My hand tightened around my great-grandmother's old tarot deck. I didn't remember bringing it. I toyed with the idea of letting the cards decide.

before:
The youth knelt on the crimson spiralgrass, her aqua skin catching the filtered dawn light that sifted through the mated-pair veil-canopy. The Dohkar’s hand shot out and seized the girl by the wrist before she could finish the second repetition, yanking her upright so the veil-canopy shuddered above them all. “Name the father now or the rite collapses,” the Dohkar demanded, voice cracking across the clearing like a snapped tether.

I lunged forward through the ring of First Favored, ceremonial sash whipping against my thighs, and planted myself between the Dohkar and the girl. My fingers closed around the girl’s free arm and pulled her back toward the spiralgrass, forcing her knees down again before the alignment could fracture further. Heat flared under my aqua skin where the Dohkar’s grip had brushed mine, a live current that made my breath hitch once, sharp and shallow, as every eye swung to measure the interference.

“Release her,” I said, the words raw without the gossamer band. “The offer stands as discipline alone.” The comm-link at my belt flared again, Julian’s voice cutting through the sudden silence with a single clipped syllable of my name that landed like a brand between my shoulder blades. The Dohkar’s Weave-Script flared crimson and he stepped closer, the mated-pair canopy rippling as if the entire clearing leaned in to witness the breach. I held my ground, one palm lifted to block the advancing guests while the other stayed locked on the girl’s shoulder, refusing to let the lineage claim surface in the open air.

Murmurs swelled into open accusation. A First Favored lunged sideways to block the exit path, her gossamer sleeve brushing my cheek as she hissed that the supervisor had broken protocol for personal gain. The girl trembled under my hand but stayed silent, her earlier gift now a live wire twisting between us. I turned my head just enough to meet the Dohkar’s stare and spoke again, louder, naming the discipline requirement as the only acceptable bargain, forcing the assembly to choose between accepting the corrected rite or declaring the entire veil-canopy void on the spot.

Julian’s name surfaced once more from the comm-link, this time threaded with an urgency that pulled at the edge of my attention even as the Dohkar raised both hands to halt the crowd. The girl’s shallow breath hit my forearm, warm and rapid, while the spiralgrass blades beneath us began to coil tighter in response to the failed alignment. I refused to step back, instead shifting my weight forward to claim the center of the clearing, every movement declaring that the rite would continue under my terms or not at all. The Dohkar’s voice dropped to a growl. “Then finish it yourself, supervisor, before the Chayr arrives to witness what you have already exposed.”
